title: Verifiable-reward RL (GRPO-style, toy)
paper: Shao et al. 2024, DeepSeekMath (GRPO); DeepSeek-AI 2025, DeepSeek-R1
claim: A policy can be improved with a rule-checkable reward and group-relative advantages (reward minus the group mean, divided by the group std), with no value network and no reward model.
setup: A GRU encoder-decoder trained from scratch (no pretraining) on single-digit addition. Per step 32 prompts x 16 samples, reward 1 iff the answer is exactly right, 400 on-policy steps, lr 0.003, 5 seeds. 20 of 100 (a, b) pairs are held out and never trained on.
result: Greedy accuracy on training pairs 0.3% -> 30.2% ± 9.8; on held-out pairs 0.0% -> 2.0% ± 2.7.
verdict_reason: Training accuracy rises by 30.0 points (3.1x seed std), so the mechanism learns from a verifiable reward alone. Held-out gain is 2.0 points: it mostly memorises training pairs rather than learning addition.
mismatches: A toy task and a from-scratch GRU, not a pretrained LLM: this shows the mechanism, not reasoning emergence.
No clipping or KL term: updates are exactly on-policy (one step per batch), unlike full GRPO.
The paper's gains come from large pretrained models; no 'aha' behaviour can appear here.
Held-out generalisation is weak, so the learned policy is largely a lookup of seen pairs.
